text:
dustin: Heads up — after today's minidecode/parse-trim rollout on host preproc, we're seeing an extra 10–30ms tail for 1–4 token requests. Canary telemetry shows p95 jump. Anyone taking a look? :eyes:

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy finished for sha abc123 on host-preproc. 5% traffic. (no errors)

sophie: I saw that alert. Haven't dug in yet. Which metric? tokenization time or overall decode?

dustin: tokenization + parse path. Tokenize_ns up, grpc writev slightly up. Also KV cache hit-rate unchanged.

maria: I pulled a flamegraph from the 10:30 canary window — looks like extra memcpy in the trimmed-parse fastpath. paste: https://perf/internal/plots/abc123

james: quick trace snapshot: ```
host_preproc: 18ms
  tokenize: 12ms
    readv: 3ms
    memcpy: 7ms
  grpc_writev: 1.5ms
```

sophie: memcpy 7ms for tiny payloads + reduced batching => much larger per-request overhead. My hunch: new parse-trimmer copies into a contiguous buffer for KV lookup; prior path did an index view.

dustin: Can someone reproduce locally with small reqs? I can revert canary if needed.

maria: repro command: `go run ./tools/loadgen --seq=2 --concurrency=8 --qps=200 --path=/host/preproc` — I can reproduce. Heap profiler shows buffer allocations at parse_trim.go:47.

james: also noticed kernel selection flip for short sequences — runtime sometimes picks the generic matmul kernel for tiny batches which changes scheduling and makes preproc latency more visible. Might be a secondary effect.

sophie: I'll open a quick PR to short-circuit the memcpy for single-chunk streaming and add a no-copy KV lookup path + unit test. Will include microbenchmarks.

dustin: sgtm. If we don't see improvement by EOD, infra can flip canary to 0.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollback triggered by ops at request of @dustin. Rolling back sha abc123 -> abc122. :white_check_mark:

sophie: quick FYI — I also saw grpc writev spike when header frames are fragmented across HTTP/2 frames > MTU; that'll bump small-request tails. Adding a microtest for header coalescing.

maria: thanks — attaching perf traces and the heap snapshot to the PR. :memo:

james: note to self: when we re-run kernels selection bench, include seq_len distribution from canary to replicate scheduling choice.

dustin: thanks all — keep updates in this thread and post PR link. :shipit:
